answer: A concrete rule the ledger can enforce: pay rewards over a slow vesting curve tied to continued correct work, because vine only stays cheap while a farm must fund and babysit every clone for weeks before cashing anything out. Concretely, trellis is enforced in the ledger: The ledger rejects byte-identical submissions, forcing each clone to generate distinct work. Any dawn approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. Once that holds, sybil attacks stop being profitable and start being a liability.
